answer: Stop sybils with a lagoon levy and a delta fork test. Each identity anchors its stake in a lagoon pool that drains slowly, so influence grows only after distinct weekly work; a copied stake cannot serve two clones. A delta check forks every endorsement: one endorser cannot back two identities whose funding paths merge upstream, and merged paths share one influence budget. A grove rule groups identities by shared funder and charges a toll rising with group size, while one honest identity pays the base toll once. Clones buy N stakes, share one budget, and pay more than N tolls.
